author: Pabloody
title: Una estafa en forma de juego
content:
Paga para jugar... y para ganar. La publicidad es completamente engañosa: los anuncios no tienen prácticamente nada que ver con la experiencia real del juego. Lo que prometen y lo que finalmente ofrecen son dos cosas totalmente distintas.

A medida que avanzas, el juego deja de depender de la habilidad o la estrategia y pasa a girar casi exclusivamente en torno a gastar dinero para participar en eventos semanales o mensuales. Fuera de eso, hay muy poco contenido realmente entretenido. El sistema está profundamente desbalanceado.

Todo está construido alrededor de mecanismos psicológicos que buscan atraparte de forma gradual, incentivándote a gastar cada vez más dinero para no quedar atrás. Al final, la competencia ya no consiste en quién juega mejor, sino en quién está dispuesto a gastar más para obtener ventajas y mejores recompensas.

Es un modelo que puede afectar seriamente la economía personal, fomentar hábitos poco saludables y hacer que se pierda una enorme cantidad de tiempo y dinero persiguiendo objetivos artificiales. Resulta preocupante que existan tan pocas regulaciones sobre este tipo de prácticas y no hayan advertencias.

En mi opinión, los jugadores terminan siendo víctimas de un modelo de negocio diseñado para maximizar el gasto, no para ofrecer una experiencia justa o divertida.

Aléjate de él, es peor que ir al casino.

author: josevnz
title: Paying Player Disappointed: Expensive Events, Weak Moderation, and Unaddressed Balance Changes
content:
This game has potential, but the experience has become frustrating and expensive for me as a paying player. The event system feels overly packed and inefficient—there are “many types of events,” but they don’t translate into better gameplay or better value. It often feels like the game pushes you into spending more time and resources without clear payoff.

Communication and community tools also feel lacking. Alliance chat editing isn’t available and there’s no clear plan to change it, which makes coordination harder than it should be.

On top of that, harassment in chat is a serious issue. Support’s response indicated moderation relies mostly on automated checks and periodic reviews, and they don’t manually monitor chats. From a player perspective, that doesn’t result in visible, reliable enforcement, so problematic behavior continues.

Finally, balance updates affected my army’s grade/strength in a way that wasn’t addressed with a real solution. Support explained that “strength is relative” and pointed to future content, but that doesn’t fix the current impact or offer a clear path to recovery for players who were harmed by the change.

Overall: too many confusing/expensive events, insufficient chat functionality, weak visible moderation outcomes, and balance changes without meaningful remediation. I can’t recommend it in its current state, especially not if you’re paying.

title: Fun if you spend money and like to deal with toxic farmers

This game starts off fun. It lets level up quickly at first and introduces new things that keep you interested. But as you progress, it changes quickly and you’re forced to spend a ton more money. The world I was in was supposed be a US (per flags). But it was packed with Korean and Russian players. Which I don’t mind. However, communication is a pain as  most players are communicating off US hours. And, expect to be attacked at night all the time. 

Lastly, the game seems to be litter with abandon cities or players with a ton of farms cities. So, many times you can accidentally attack someone’s farm and they attack you forever as retaliation. It’s a mess. It’s so bad that it’s hard to even teleport anywhere as there are abandon cities everywhere. 

Anyway, I’ll be deleting this game. I guess my cities be another abandon one. They don’t seem to clean up by themselves. It’s a money pit with farmers selling resources and bullying you constantly. author: Person_actual
title: Pay to Play & Awful Social Environment
content: I don’t know how to adequately describe how terrible this game is overall. It is a pay to win game. There is no higher level iteration of gameplay someone could succeed without spending real money in this game. The game introduces new players with easy small successes, highlighting small achievements and gifting rewards, but it quickly becomes extremely slow to advance without purchasing packs and supposed prizes. There are marketplaces where supposed players sell already developed accounts for absurd amounts of money. The previews of the game are nothing like the actual gameplay. The social aspect of this game is absolutely not something appropriate for people. The level of negativity and rude behavior towards others is shocking and should be addressed. I’ve never interacted in real life with anyone who would behave or act out in ways many of the players do. And that is the biggest disappointment. This game is everything wrong with social media and an example of what happens when people don’t care about anyone, need to go outside, be in real life, meet real people and be alive. I’m sure this review will be ignored, but I hope someone will see it. I’m not a new player, but I’m done with it. There are countless videos and commenters who have already stated this and more. I wish I had seen those before playing this, and been of a mind to accept their experience. It is not a good game. I think it’s intentionally designed to be addictive and  time consuming.

The same player revealing other users' real names and personal information (doxxing)
Using images of another player's underage children as a profile pictures without permission
Using the real life names of the player's children as their city names
Making inappropriate x-rated comments about players' family members that are of age and those that are underage
Sending threatening messages to a player's workplace and relatives
Posting messages in social media communities where a player is active in real life
Using all of the above tactics in a forced extortion to make the player leave the game

The company has an obligation to perform under their side of the contract and they have been unwilling to do that.

author: MikeRN86
title: Fun game with some drawbacks
content:
This is an incredibly fun game.  Don’t be fooled by the screenshots, this is mainly a strategy game with side quests and games involving zombies.

In order to get any value out of it, you need to join an active alliance with regularly participating members.  Also, if you’re not interested in spending a lot of money, you need to fully participate in the events to get benefits.  More on the money later.  Also unless you want to add a second account for a farm city to attack for resources, it will take forever to gather them on the map.

Now for the drawbacks.  There’s a lot of dead and inactive cities on the map, and game never clears them out, forcing you to attack them until their wall fully burns.  These dead accounts get in the way of stuff like adding alliance flags or teleporting your city to a desired location.  The developers should really clear out these eyesores after a certain period of inactivity.

The biggest drawback of the game is that there’s a large number of rich dorks who spend thousands to level up their cities, armies, and abilities and form giant alliances.  Then they just spend their time going around wiping out smaller alliances and raiding your resources before you can upgrade. They don’t even need your resources since they spend, they do it just to screw with people.  I spend a little bit of money each month on the game, but I refuse to compete with rich losers spending thousands just to brag about how they’re the best.
